questions.q: This lesson builds on Course 5's GlideRecord performance pitfalls lesson. What does it add?
options: A full replacement for everything that lesson already taught
How to recognize those same mistakes by their signature in a profiled transaction, not just by reading the script
A reason those mistakes no longer matter on modern ServiceNow instances
A new unrelated set of GlideRecord methods
questions.explain: The underlying mistakes (query-in-a-loop, missing setLimit, looping to count) were already covered; this lesson is about spotting them once you're measuring a real transaction.

questions.q: A debug panel shows: GlideRecord Query: problem [47 executions] — 2980 ms, inside one business rule transaction over 50 incidents. What does the 47 most likely indicate?
options: A database replication error
The query against problem is sitting inside a loop, running once per incident instead of once total
ServiceNow automatically re-runs every query 47 times for accuracy
47 unrelated transactions happened at the same moment
questions.explain: An execution count that close to the number of loop iterations is the signature of a query left inside the loop instead of being run once.

options: addActiveQuery() is spelled incorrectly
The incident query itself is missing a condition
A brand-new GlideRecord query against problem runs once per incident in the loop, instead of once total
while (incGr.next()) never terminates
questions.explain: Opening and querying probGr inside the while loop means that query runs for every incident returned by the outer query.

questions.q: What is the real fix for that code, given that problem_id is a reference field already on the incident record?
options: Add a GlideAggregate instead of the inner GlideRecord
Remove the outer query entirely
Dot-walk the reference field (incGr.problem_id.number) instead of opening a new GlideRecord per iteration
Increase the response-time threshold on the Slow Request Log
questions.explain: Dot-walking a reference field already on the current record reads the related record's fields without issuing a brand-new query each time.

questions.q: A script runs 'var gr = new GlideRecord("incident"); ... while (gr.next()) { count++; }' just to produce a count. What should replace this pattern?
options: GlideAggregate, with addAggregate('COUNT') and getAggregate('COUNT')
A second nested GlideRecord loop
Removing the addActiveQuery() call
Calling .get() instead of .query()
questions.explain: GlideAggregate asks the database to compute the count directly, instead of fetching every full row just to increment a counter in script.
